summary.text: 考 is commonly used for “examine” or “test.” A favored historical analysis builds it from reduced 老 and 丂, but the relationship between its recorded “father” and “consider” uses and its current meaning is unresolved.

formation.text: The favored analysis treats 考 as phonosemantic: reduced 老 contributes an “old/elder” category, while 丂 marks a sound. A competing analysis proposes that 丂 was first used for “father” and 老 was later added as a classifier.

components.text: 耂 is analyzed as reduced 老, with the lower 匕 omitted; in the favored account it contributes the category “old/elder.”
丂 has a proposed phonetic role in 考. Its earlier pictorial interpretation is disputed: proposals include a branch, a cane or staff, and an axe handle, and its original name is not established.

sound_limitation.text: The recorded Middle Chinese and Mandarin matches provide real comparisons, but the reported Old Chinese forms differ and were not independently verified; the later matches alone cannot confirm the ancient phonetic relation.

sound.text: Both are recorded with Middle Chinese khawX; their reported Old Chinese reconstructions differ, so this comparison alone does not establish the ancient sound relation.
Both are recorded with Mandarin kǎo; this modern match alone does not establish the ancient sound relation.

history.text: One proposed graphic account says early Western Zhou writing used 老 for both “old” and “father,” then added 丂 to distinguish 考, often omitting 老’s lower 匕. A competing account reverses that construction: 丂 was used for “father” first, with 老 added as a classifier.

Reported bronze examples use 考 for “father” and “consider/estimate.” Other examples use the graph for the sounds of 孝 and 巧. These reports do not date the examples or establish a progression among the uses.
攷 is listed as a variant of 考, but the timing and graphic history of their relationship are not specified.

uncertainties.text: Because 丂’s depicted object and original name are disputed, an account in which its graph was borrowed for “father” through a sound match remains uncertain.
The reported examples do not establish the earliest dates of the “father” and “consider/estimate” uses or a semantic development between them and “examine/test.”

The shared Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings of 丂 and 考 coexist with distinct reported Old Chinese reconstructions; those reconstructions were not independently verified against the inspected table.

senses.text: A traditional lexicographic analysis glosses 考 as “old”; whether that was the graph’s earliest meaning is unresolved.
Reported bronze examples use 考 for “father,” often but not always referring to a deceased father.
A reported bronze example uses 考 for “consider/estimate”; its date and relation to the “father” sense are unresolved.
The supplied definitions give the current sense “examine, test; investigate.” Its chronology relative to the reported historical uses is unresolved.

limitations.text: The available glosses and reported examples do not establish a chronology or semantic transitions among “old,” “father,” “consider/estimate,” and current “examine/test.”

overview.text: 考 is commonly used for “examine” or “test.” A favored analysis combines reduced 老, meaning “old/elder,” with 丂 as a sound marker; its historical “father” use does not by itself explain the current meaning.

components.text: 耂 is reduced 老; in the favored analysis, it contributes the category “old/elder.”
丂 has a proposed sound role, but its pictured object and original name remain disputed.

relationships.text: In the favored analysis, 耂 is reduced 老 and contributes the “old/elder” category; the competing account treats 老 as a classifier added to 丂.

Traditional and favored inscriptional analyses assign 丂 a sound role. Shared Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings are reported, but differing reported Old Chinese forms and uncertainty about 丂 limit what those comparisons establish.
攷 is listed as a variant of 考; the timing and fuller history of their overlap are unresolved.
